The closest match is a study on maximizing revenue for batteries and electrolysers by using measured device behavior in Nordic power markets, specifically Danish electricity and ancillary service markets [1]. It explicitly models real hardware characteristics such as ramp limits, efficiency, and setpoint-tracking accuracy, then uses a price-driven optimization framework with real market data to optimize multi-market participation and daily profits [1]. The paper reports optimized daily profits for both a battery energy storage system and an electrolyser, and argues that incorporating experimental performance is important when evaluating business cases across multiple markets and years [1].

The other supplied papers do not address Nordic power exchanges for converter-like tools or electrochemical cells in this way. One focuses on automated discovery of better reconfigurable power converter topologies, improving figure of merit and efficiency rather than market income optimization [10], while another is about battery power prediction in electric vehicles, not market participation [2].
